- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline at 10–15% below peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is trending up, model often underestimates upside — add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility in sentiment-driven markets — smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce noise.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.5 to -0.5 in 2–3 days), model tends to lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts mean reversion — reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative over last 7 days.
